_doc: WPC Excessive Rainfall Outlook. Risk = smoothed (window rain / FFG); FFG lowered by antecedent rain from the 'pre' part of rain_config. ratio_thresholds are illustrative proxies for the 5/15/30/50% categories. text = discussion (one paragraph per string).

headlines: THERE IS A HIGH RISK OF EXCESSIVE RAINFALL ACROSS PORTIONS OF NORTH GEORGIA AND EAST-CENTRAL ALABAMA...INCLUDING THE ATLANTA METROPOLITAN AREA
THERE IS A MODERATE RISK OF EXCESSIVE RAINFALL ACROSS PORTIONS OF EAST ALABAMA...WEST-CENTRAL GEORGIA...SOUTHEAST TENNESSEE...AND THE SOUTHERN APPALACHIANS
regions: North Georgia, East Alabama, and the Southern Appalachians

A High Risk was issued across north Georgia, including metro Atlanta, and east-central Alabama in coordination with WFOs FFC, BMX, GSP, and MRX and the Southeast River Forecast Center. After three days of the predecessor rain event, storm totals are 7 to 11 inches along the axis, including about 10 inches at Atlanta Hartsfield-Jackson. Three-hour FFG is below 1 inch across much of the metro and below 1.5 inches over most of north Georgia.

The predecessor rain event will continue into this afternoon before Hurricane Delphine arrives tonight. Delphine is forecast to make landfall on the Florida Panhandle this evening and race north along the Georgia-Alabama line at 45 to 55 mph, passing west of Atlanta around 2 AM EDT Saturday. Its forward speed will limit totals at any one point to 3 to 6 inches. However, rain rates of 1 to 2.5 inches per hour in the core and right-front quadrant will exceed guidance nearly everywhere on this saturated ground. Considerable to catastrophic flash flooding is expected, including life-threatening urban flooding in the Atlanta metro overnight.

A Moderate Risk surrounds the High Risk into the southern Appalachians, where upslope flow late tonight will enhance rainfall on already wet slopes. The Slight Risk reaches the Florida Panhandle coast near landfall, where FFG is higher.
